results.title: Recursive self-improvement - Wikipedia
results.snippet: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is a hypothetical process in which an artificial intelligence (AI) system iteratively designs a more capable successor. results.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
results.snippet: Oct 7, 2026 · RSIGym exposes training, inference, rollout, evaluation, and sandbox execution through reusable services, with shared budget and permission controls supporting Data, Harness, and Joint improvement tracks.

results.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
results.snippet: RSIGym gives a research agent reusable tools to generate data, train models, evaluate candidates, and revise execution harnesses. The agent chooses the experiments; the platform handles the infrastructure, permissions, and service budget.

results.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
results.snippet: Recursive self-improvement requires carrying accepted changes into later improvement cycles, while studying agent-proposed changes also requires substantial research infrastructure.

results.title: RSIGym: An Environment Built for Agents to Improve AI Systems
results.snippet: Oct 8, 2026 · The vision of Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) is for AI to act as an agent that can sustain its own research: identify capability bottlenecks in itself or a target system, propose hypotheses for improvement, design and run experiments, and use the results to decide what to try next.
